Sharma, Speak the truth as it is—don't twist facts to suit any ideology.

If You say Education Minister is only  bad element  and modi  government has done a great job, then people have the right to ask questions too. What happened to the promises of 100 smart cities? Where is NEP? Why is road quality still poor in many places? Why have thousands of schools reportedly been closed or merged? What about the promise of doubling farmers' income? Why do paper leaks continue to happen? Why has freebie politics become a competition across parties?

A healthy democracy is not about blindly supporting the government or blindly opposing it. The media's job is to question those in power because they are the ones making decisions today. The opposition should also be questioned, but when a government has been in power for many years and enjoys a strong majority, accountability must primarily be directed toward those who govern.

This message is not only for supporters of the current government. It is also for sections of the media and political groups on the other side that only highlight failures while ignoring achievements. Selective outrage is not journalism; it is propaganda.

The nation is bigger than the Right or the Left. Patriotism is not about defending politicians; it is about defending truth, accountability, and the interests of the people. Ask questions without fear, appreciate good work where it exists, and criticize failures where they occur.

Don't sell the country for political loyalty. The country comes first—always.
